1 	Deltapath REST API Documentation
This document demonstrates how developers can manage call center operations, virtual meetings,
audio conferencing, and much more via the Deltapath REST API. Each operation listed below
includes all available parameters and showcases various examples to help you understand each
function.
1.1 	Understanding Basic Concepts
Deltapath’s REST API uses an XML encoding over HTTP and HTTPS transport. The API adheres to
a Representational State Transfer (REST) architecture. This document assumes the reader has a
basic understanding of XML, HTTP, and HTTPS, but may unfamiliar with REST.
1.1.1 	Resources and HTTP Methods
Each data object accessible through the API is modeled as a resource. Some example resources are
call center, conference, numbering plan, and virtual meeting. Each resource is uniquely identified
by a URL and is referenced by means of a URL path.
You may access the API and manipulate resources by using standard REST conventions. Each API
method is invoked using one of the following HTTP methods:
Ø 	GET – performs a read operation.
• 	This operation returns a representation of a resource. GET is guaranteed to
be a “safe” operation. It will never modify the state of the system. GET
typically takes no input except the resource URL, and typically returns HTTP
headers and an XML document as output.
Ø 	POST – performs a create operation.
• 	This operation creates a new resource. The POST method may also be used
for operations that modify the state of a system but are typically more
complex than simply updating a resource state. POST normally takes an
XML document as input and returns only HTTP headers as output.
Ø 	PUT – performs an update operation.
• 	This operation replaces the data for a resource with a new set of data. PUT
typically takes an XML document as input and returns only HTTP headers as
output.
Ø 	DELETE – performs a delete operation.
• 	This operation removes a resource from the system. DELETE typically takes
no input except the resource URL, and returns only HTTP headers as output.
All four HTTP methods are not always available for each resource. For example, some
resources may only support GET.
1.2 	General Usage
A token is required for every request that is sent to the Deltapath REST API. Please see frSIP - API
Token Request for information on how to obtain a token.
"X-frSIP-API-Token":
"a971afb62a8ba84f5d1cc1f43e2facf156147091fbe09bd80f8bcdad6344bd33"

28.13 	Call Attend Transfer (v1.0.0)
Forward a call to another destination while the original destination remains attended
POST
/RESTful/index.php/[v1/post/]frsipswitchboard/call/attendtransfer
28.13.1 	Parameter
Field 	Type 	Description
pchannelid 	String 	The source channel
rchannelid 	String 	The destination channel
transferto 	String 	The destination phone book number
calleridnum
(optional) String Optional caller id number; It can be customized and
will be displayed at the destination
calleridname
(optional) String Optional caller id name; same as
&quot;calleridnum&quot;
accountcode
(optional) String Optional, a call accounting account code, it must be a
valid mailbox number
customvariable
(optional) String Optional, a custom vairable set to both channel using
FRSIP-CUSTOMIZABLE-DATA
calltype 	String
The type of transfer: either &quot;incoming&quot; or
&quot;outgoing&quot;, its usage is as following:
Suppose we have channel A talking to channel B,
then A is the semantic 'source' while B is the
semantic 'dest.'. 1. If we specify
<code>calltype</code> to be &quot;incoming&quot;,
then we must specify <code>pchannelid</code> to
be channel A and <code>rchannelid</code> to be
channel B 2. If we specify <code>calltype</code> to
be &quot;outgoing&quot;, then we must specify
<code>pchannelid</code> to be channel B and
<code>rchannelid</code> to be channel A Basically
this param is used to determine which channel should
be used as the logical source for this API (not from
the end-user's perspective)
credential (optional) 	String 	Deprecated, currently not used
mac (optional) 	String 	Deprecated, currently not used

exten 	String 	The extension number to spy on
device (optional) 	String Optional; The device name of the target user
(extension) that is going to be spied on
options (optional) 	String
Optional; The spy option, accepts the following
values: '' - param set but empty 'w' - single char lower
case w 'B' - single char upper case B Together with
optional <code>channelId</code>, the following
combinations are allowed: Suppose we have channel
A and B, such that A has an outgoing call to B,
furthermore, we use User C's extension and device
for each request, then the following holds 1. options
'w', channelId &lt;A's channel&gt;: Whisper Src. 2.
options 'w', channelId &lt;B's channel&gt;: Whisper
Dest. 3. options '', channelId &lt;B's channel&gt; :
Listen In B 4. options 'B', channelId &lt;B's
channel&gt; : Barge In B 5. options '', channelId '':
Keep Listen In 6. options 'B', channelId '': Keep Barge
In All of the above combinations assume the same
<code>exten</code> and <code>device</code>
being used in each request
extraChannel
(optional) String 	Deprecated, no longer used
redirect (optional) 	Bool 	Deprecated, no longer used
28.37.1.1 	Request-Example:
/RESTful/index.php/frsipswitchboard/call/spy

values, it optionally takes: - 'abnormal', filter by
'status' == 'Critical' or 'Warning' - 'las', filter by
<code>id</code> NOT IN (mainId, bkId[0])

<code>true</code> to disable the sorting inside this
function, and keep the result list un-sliced; If unset, it
is treated as <code>false</code>.
includeTZ
(optional) Boolean
<code>true</code> to include server timezone in all
datetime values ; If unset, it is treated as
<code>false</code>.
